conditions_and_exclusions: Announcement No. 10 of 2025 lists specified tungsten, tellurium, bismuth, molybdenum and indium items and associated production technology; descriptions include specific forms, characteristics and thresholds.

records.restriction_type: export licensing for selected rare-earth items
conditions_and_exclusions: Announcement No. 18 of 2025 lists selected items relating to samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium and yttrium.

Specified alloys, compounds, targets and some permanent magnetic materials are listed, including samarium-cobalt permanent magnetic materials and neodymium-iron-boron permanent magnetic materials containing terbium or dysprosium. Exporters must apply for a licence and identify controlled items when declaring goods.
records.reported_effect: Export licensing and customs declaration requirements apply to the specified controlled items; the announcement does not establish a case-study shipment delay.

records.restriction_type: advanced computing integrated circuit due diligence and export licensing controls
conditions_and_exclusions: The Bureau of Industry and Security rule revises controls and due diligence for certain advanced computing integrated circuits and related transactions.
The rule is effective 16 January 2025; compliance with the newly revised EAR text was not required until 31 January 2025. Pre-existing requirements are not covered by that grace period.
Licensing and exceptions depend on the precise item, transaction, parties and regulatory criteria; review the original rule and subsequent amendments.
records.reported_effect: The rule introduced revised compliance, due-diligence and licensing provisions for covered transactions; no actual case-study shipment delay is established.

records.restriction_type: catch-all controls on specified advanced AI chips
conditions_and_exclusions: A reviewed legal commentary reports that Directive No. 1/2025 covers specified unlisted advanced AI chips and technical criteria under the Strategic Trade Act 2010.

The commentary states that, effective 14 July 2025, at least 30 days' advance notice is required where a person knows or reasonably suspects a restricted activity, and a permit is required if the authority allows the transaction.
The same commentary notes uncertainty over whether authorities require notification more broadly; the directive's described scope is not expressly limited to US-origin chips.
records.reported_effect: The reported directive adds a conditional notification and permit process for covered export, transshipment or transit; no particular case-study transaction or delay is established.

source.licence_notes: Source redistribution terms not verified; concise attributed summary and link only.

limitations: The official announcement page returned no substantive text in the reviewed fetch; the primary directive and technical annex were not independently reviewed.

The government statement as reproduced by Bernama describes permits for US-origin chips more broadly; legal commentary distinguishes the directive's restricted-activity trigger and notes implementation uncertainty.
Multiple category codes and exceptions apply, so no single product classification is recorded. Do not infer the rule applies to all semiconductors or all trade.
No verified end date, complete amendment history, case-study product, supplier, permit decision or shipment delay is established.

search_window.note: Search interval uses the effective date reported by legal commentary through the case-study cutoff; it does not assert continued unchanged effect or expiry.

records.restriction_type: Section 301 port-entry fees on China-linked vessels
conditions_and_exclusions: Fees applied to certain Chinese-built vessels, vessels with Chinese owners or operators, and foreign-built vehicle carriers calling at US ports.

USTR suspended the actions for one year from 10 November 2025 after the 1 November US-China trade announcement; China suspended its reciprocal special port fees on US-linked vessels for the same period.
records.reported_effect: Holland & Knight reported that the fees took effect on 14 October 2025 and were suspended from 10 November 2025 for one year.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not independently verified; concise attributed summary and source link only.

limitations: Fee amounts, exemptions and the USTR Federal Register notices were not reviewed. effective_to is the last day before the suspension, not a repeal; the fees could resume when the suspension ends.

A single law-firm source says the suspension was set to be extended to 9 January 2027 after a September 2026 summit; not confirmed against an official source: https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/5jbjuiqd/section-301-port-fees-on-chinese-vessels.pdf.
The fees attach to the vessel, not the cargo's origin. The affected_countries link to China-country suppliers is location context only; see approximations.
No case-study vessel's ownership, build country or fee liability, and no cost passed to a shipment, has been established.

approximations.basis: Analyst approximation: the measure targets China's maritime sector through vessel build, ownership and operation. Cargo of any origin on a covered vessel could bear the cost, and Chinese-origin cargo on other vessels would not.

search_window.note: The period the fees were in effect before the suspension.
